&of the tatnes of the earth aboundance of corne and wine. 29. And let
peoples ſerue thee, and tribes adore thee: be thou Lord of thy brethren,
and thv mothers children bow they before thee. He that ſhal curſe
thee, be he curſed: and he that ſhal bleſſe thee, be he repleni :hecl with
bleſſings. 20. Iſaac had ſcarce ended his words , and Iacob now gone
forth abroad, but Eſau came, 21. and brought in to his father meats
made of his hunting , ſaving: Ariſe my tather, and eate ot thy ſonnes
huntiug ; that thy ſoule may bleffe me. 32. And Iſaac ſaid to him: Why!
who art thou? Who anſwered : I am thy firſt begotten ſonne Eſau.
33. Iſaac was amared and aſtonished exceedingly, and matueling
more then a man can belieue, ſaid: Who is he then that euen now
tratified that he brought me veniſon that he had taken, and I did eate of al things
had done.

Rightly is his name called Iacob : tor he hath ſupplanted me loe the
ſecond time: tv firſt. birth-right he tooke betore, and now the ſecond
timne he hath ſtollen my bleſſing. And egaine to his father he ſaid:
Haſt thou not reſerued me alſo a bleſſing? 37. Iſaac anſwered : I haue
appointed him thy Lord, and al his brethren I haue made ſubiect to his
ſeruice: with corne and wine I haue eſtabliſhed him, and tor thee, mv

he wept that he howled againe, 29. Iſaac being moued, ſaid to him:
In (4) the fat of the earth, and in the deaw of heauen from aboue
40. shal thy bleſſing be. Thou shalt liue by the ſword, and shalt ſerue
thy brother: and (e) the time shal come, when thou :halt shake off
and looſe his voak fromn thy neck. 41. Eſau therfore alwaies hated
Iacob for the bleſſing wherewith, his father had bleſſed him : and he
ſaid is his hart : The daies wil come ot the mourning ot my father, and
